items_missed: Never confirmed or used the customer's name — Kaitlyn's name is not spoken once in the entire call, even though the customer used the rep's name ('Thank you so much Bree')
No structured agenda statement — 'before I go through how everything works' is not a roadmap; no 'I'll gather details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes'
No 'Sound good?' confirmation to close the agenda
Never checked/announced availability for the Sept 30 date — only confirmed it was the requested date
Never asked about packing services (customer is a first-time mover explicitly asking 'how this all works')
Never asked how many boxes they'd have
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked about additional rooms — garage, storage unit, balcony/patio
'No hidden fees' pitch was partial — covered transportation and assembly fees but not credit card fees or fuel surcharge
Estimate variables incomplete — no equivalents/school-bus style reference, and never tied the specialty items (three TVs, ball python tank + stand) or bed disassembly to move time
Save Your Ass speech had no consolidation examples — no kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, or photos off walls

Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Never asked the customer to reply with corrections to verify the details
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' at the close
Never gave business hours or how to reach the team
top_strength: The differentiator block was complete and well-delivered — No Worries $2,000 coverage explicitly contrasted against competitors' 60¢/lb state minimum, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee all landed in one clean sequence. She also read the customer's shopping-around comment perfectly and coached her on what hidden fees to look for at other companies, which is exactly the right competitive move.
coaching_note: This call was sold but never closed. Bri did the hard part — full differentiators, clean clock explanation, a 6-7 hour estimate with the reasoning shown, no deposit — and then handed the booking back to the customer: 'give us a callback or you can respond to the email that you would like to book.' A first-time mover who said Einstein is the highest-rated company in San Antonio was ready to be asked. She should have said 'I've got Wednesday the 30th open right now, and since there's no deposit and no cancellation fee, there's zero risk in locking it in — want me to put you on the schedule?' Second, related fix: use the customer's name. Kaitlyn's name never appears once in 11.7 minutes while the customer used Bri's name twice.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm language ('Not a problem at all', 'Absolutely', 'Of course') and a genuine rapport moment when she validated the customer's confusion over the walk-distance question, though zero use of the customer's name and several rushed, garbled stretches keep it short of Outstanding.
